intro: Build the diagram, then let the model test it.

widget.instructions: Add each force with Precise controls, choose who exerts it, then set its size and direction. The block slides up at a steady speed; press Play to see what your diagram predicts.

stem: A {{m}} kg block is pushed up a smooth (frictionless) plank tilted at {{theta}}°. Your hand pushes parallel to the plank and the block moves up at a constant speed. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
Draw every force acting on the block, with its size and direction.
answerText: Weight {{W}} N down; normal {{N}} N perpendicular to the plank; push {{P}} N up the plank.

hints.text: What touches the block? The plank and your hand. Gravity acts too. Is anything else pushing it?
Constant speed means the net force is zero. Tilt the axes and balance the forces along and across the plank.
Across the plank: N = mg cos θ. Along it: push = mg sin θ. There is no separate force for the motion itself.

extra-force-of-motion.text: There is no separate 'force of motion'. The block keeps moving at a steady speed because the forces balance. Ask of each arrow: what is pushing or pulling?

args.text: Every force needs an agent: Earth, plank or hand.

normal-equals-weight.text: On a slope the plank pushes back only against the part of the weight pressing into it: N = mg cos θ, not mg.

constant-velocity-unbalanced.text: At constant speed the push along the plank must exactly balance the weight's component down the plank, mg sin θ. Your diagram predicts the block speeding up or slowing down.

missing-weight.text: Every body near the Earth has a weight, mg, straight down.

missing-normal.text: The plank pushes on the block, perpendicular to its surface. Without it the block would sink into the plank.

missing-push.text: Your hand pushes the block up along the plank.

normal-direction.text: The normal force is perpendicular to the plank, not straight up.

push-direction.text: The push is parallel to the plank, up the slope.

double-counted-force.text: Each agent here gives one force. Remove the duplicate.

generic.text: List the agents (Earth, plank, hand), give each one force, and check that the net force is zero for a steady speed.

workedSolution.text: Weight: {{W}} N straight down, from the Earth.
Use axes along and across the plank. Across it, nothing accelerates: N = mg cos {{theta}}° = {{N}} N.
Along it, the speed is constant, so the push balances mg sin {{theta}}° = {{P}} N. No other force acts; press Play to see the steady motion.

generic.front: A block pushed up a smooth slope at constant speed: which forces act?
generic.back: Weight (down), normal (perpendicular to the slope) and the push (along it). No 'force of motion'.
